title: Peekaboo and Mirrors
strapline: Now you see me — faces, surprise and the beginnings of self.
intent: Peekaboo teaches that people and things still exist when hidden — early object permanence.
The back-and-forth of peekaboo is a baby's first turn-taking "conversation".
Mirrors help babies notice and delight in their own reflection and build a sense of self.
Sharing these games with a trusted adult deepens the key-person bond.
Anticipating the "boo!" builds joyful connection and emotional warmth.
implementation: Play peekaboo warmly and often, following the baby's cues for more or a pause.
Use cloths, hands, books and furniture to hide and reappear, naming what happens.
Place safe baby mirrors at floor level and during tummy time for babies to explore.
Talk about what the baby sees: "that's you! there's your nose".
Let the baby lead the rhythm — wait for their gaze and vocal reply before the next "boo".
Share the games one-to-one so each baby gets your full, delighted attention.
key_questions: Where has it gone — is it still there?
Who is that in the mirror?
Shall we do it again? (following the baby's reply)
Can you find my face behind the cloth?

impact.text: Babies show they know a hidden person or object still exists.
Babies take turns in a to-and-fro exchange, waiting for a reply.
Babies notice and explore their own reflection with growing interest.
Babies build a warm bond with their key person through shared play.
Babies anticipate the familiar refrain and show delighted connection.

enhancements: Safe, unbreakable baby mirrors at floor and tummy-time level.
Soft cloths, scarves and lift-the-flap books for hiding games.
A cosy one-to-one space free from noise and rush.
Family photos at baby height to name familiar faces.
A treasure basket with a mirror-backed lid to discover.
Time in the routine for unhurried, responsive play.

playing_exploring: Babies explore appearing and disappearing, and their own reflection, with all their senses.
active_learning: Babies show sustained delight and keep the game going with their key person.
creating_thinking: Babies begin to expect what happens next and anticipate the reappearance.
